[01:15:26] parallel, and 128 data parallel.
[01:15:29] Big data parallel splits.
[01:15:31] And then at the very end, because they want a long context
[01:15:33] model, they do long context extension.
[01:15:35] And for this, they crank up the context parallel,
[01:15:38] lower the data parallel.
[01:15:39] And that's how they parallelize this very memory hungry stage
[01:15:42] for long context extension.
[01:15:44] And notice, we're in tensor parallel,
[01:15:45] not export parallel land.
[01:15:47] Because Llama3 405B is a gigantic dense model.
[01:15:50] It's not a MoE model.
[01:15:54] And as a side note, right, one thing that I don't talk about,
[01:15:57] but if you, for example, become an infra engineer at one
[01:16:00] of these companies, you'll notice
[01:16:02] is GPUs fail all the time.
[01:16:05] Apparently during Llama3 405B training, GPUs failed 148 times.
[01:16:12] And so you need lots of not just fast parallelism,
[01:16:16] you need redundancy in order to be
[01:16:18] able to deal with all these kind of horrible things
[01:16:20] that can happen to your training.
[01:16:21] So there's a distributed systems challenge as well.
[01:16:25] Gamma 2, which is a Google open source model,
[01:16:29] has FSDP plus tensor parallel and sequence parallel
[01:16:34] and uses these two strategies only.
[01:16:36] And the reason why I brought up Gamma 2
[01:16:39] is, as far as I understand, this is basically a realization
[01:16:43] of the Google claim that for TPUs, really
[01:16:46] you don't need to do pipelines.
[01:16:48] You just take a really big toroidal mesh
[01:16:50] and you tensor parallel over that big mesh network
[01:16:53] that you have.
[01:16:54] Unclear whether this can scale out forever.
[01:16:57] That has always been a little bit less clear to me.
[01:17:00] But at least the gamma scales, this is definitely the case.
[01:17:04] Finally, I took a look at some of the models that were trained
[01:17:07] this year, like Mistral 8x22B, and during my investigation,
[01:17:11] one of the things that I discovered was actually
[01:17:14] if you're interested in model training and parallelism
[01:17:16] configurations in the wild, NVIDIA has a repository called
[01:17:21] Megatron Bridge, where they release a lot of recommended
[01:17:26] training configurations for a lot of different model sizes
[01:17:28] and model settings.
[01:17:30] And you can take a look at what they end up saying is the right
[01:17:33] model configuration for an 8x22B MoE or DeepSeek V3 modeling.
[01:17:40] And so for Mixtral, they do expert parallel of 8,
[01:17:43] pipeline parallel of 4, and an additional tensor parallel of 4.
[01:17:46] This one for the attention layers.
[01:17:47] And you see this follows the prescription
[01:17:50] of, keep your expert parallel roughly around eight.
[01:17:54] Nemotron 3 Super follows the DeepSeek V3 model,
[01:17:58] has a bunch of expert parallel as well as context parallel,
[01:18:00] because they were doing extensions,
[01:18:02] at least in this article.
[01:18:04] And then the last one that I want to talk about
[01:18:07] is Qwen 3, which follows the DeepSeek
[01:18:10] recipe, which is a fairly large amount of expert parallel 32.
[01:18:16] And they have eight pipeline parallel and two tensor parallel
[01:18:19] to split up things like the attention matrices.
[01:18:24] It is actually interesting to see additionally
[01:18:27] the different kinds of benchmarking
[01:18:29] that NVIDIA folks have done for parallelizing different models.
[01:18:32] And you see, I won't go into details of what this is.
[01:18:35] This is in the NVIDIA bridge repo,
[01:18:37] if you want to take a look.
[01:18:38] There's all sorts of different configurations
[01:18:40] that you can pick even within tensor parallel that
[01:18:43] can significantly affect the performance of these.
[01:18:46] So the systems integration is quite significant.
[01:18:50] So to put everything together, I decided maybe
[01:18:53] I would build an overview.
[01:18:56] Really, the thing that's common to this is as much as you can,
[01:18:59] all the models use data parallel.
[01:19:01] They maximize the data parallel domains to the extent
[01:19:03] that they can.
[01:19:05] Tensor parallel almost always remains below eight.
[01:19:08] And expert parallel can sometimes be big now.
[01:19:10] And I think that's partially because of DeepSeek V3 and a lot
[01:19:13] of the infra that they built for large scale expert parallel
[01:19:17] training.
[01:19:19] Good.
[01:19:20] OK.
[01:19:21] So to put everything together, right.
[01:19:23] The highest level point, right, of this lecture
[01:19:26] is we need to think about multi-GPU,
[01:19:29] multi-node, maybe even multi-data center parallelism.
[01:19:32] And to think about efficiency in that regime,
[01:19:34] we need to really bring to bear all the approaches that we have.
[01:19:38] Because you've got fast links, you've got slow links,
[01:19:40] you've got techniques that make use of batch sizes and all
